This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 23-07-2021 at about 7.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding the scooter bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-EQ-0492 from Chandapura, on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, carefully, cautiously and by following all the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, a Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409,
driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from behind and dashed against the scooter bearing Reg.

2 No.TN-24-AB-3750 and then dashed to the scooter of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

The Sarjapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car,
for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.

3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4.
The respondents No.1 and 2 in their written statement have denied all the allegations made in the petition.

They have contended that, as on the date of alleged accident, the Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 was having valid insurance with the respondent No.3 insurance company,
bundled long term liability policy vide policy No.991491823740007118, valid from 15-10-2020 to 14-10- 2021.
Further they have contended that, as on the date of accident, the driver of said car was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against them.
5. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of private car/third party liability only policy bearing No.991401823740007118 in favour of respondent No.2, in respect of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05- MY-5409 and it was valid from 15-10-2018 to 14-10-2021 and it was valid as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EQ- 0492 which involved in the alleged accident are not made as parties to the above proceedings.
They are the proper and necessary parties to the above proceedings to adjudicate the controversy involved between the parties in the above matter.
It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of the vehicle bearing No.KA-05-MY- 5409 as alleged in the claim petition.

Further it is contended that, the respondent No.2 had willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident.
It is clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Section 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Further it is contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492.
The rider and pillion riders who were not wearing safety headgear, was not holding driving licence to ride the said motorcycle and insurance to use the said vehicle on the public road.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further, it has sought Ravindra Alias Ravindra Kumar vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5793441/
3 permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

sentences.text: For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 23-07-2021, at about 7.00 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Toyota Innova Car bearing Reg.

No.KA-05-MY- 5409 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3.
The respondents No.1 and 3 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 23-07-2021 at about 7.00 p.m., when the petitioner was riding the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, carefully, cautiously and following all the traffic rules and regulations, at that time the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409, drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the scooter of the petitioner from behind.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.

sentences.text: Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to 12.
Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.2 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazar,

Ex.P.4 is true copy of charge- sheet, Ex.P.5 is true copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.6 is true copy of post-mortem report, Ex.P.7 is true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is radiological report, Ex.P.9 are x-rays (total 8), Ex.P.10 is discharge summary, Ex.P.11 is notarized copy of Aadhar card and Ex.P.12 are medical bills.
12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7 and 10,

facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, from behind.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.4,

has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 in the said accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.3 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.
But, the respondent No.1 to 3 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident.

Further, the respondent No.3 has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409.
But, the respondent No.3 has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1/respondent No.2,
who is none other than the owner of offending car bearing Reg. No.KA- 05-MY-5409, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that,
the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY- 5409 and dashing the same to the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ- 0492 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 42 feet wide of Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, in between the offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY- 5409, scooter bearing No.TN-24-AB-3750 and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EQ-0492 of the petitioner, which Ravindra Alias Ravindra Kumar vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5793441/
5 were proceeding in the same direction.

sentences.text: Further, it is pertinent to note that, it is not the case of the respondents that, the said accident has taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.4 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 radiological report,
Ex.P.9 x-rays (total 8) and Ex.P.10 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury in a road traffic accident.

The petitioner has sustained 1) abrasions present over the left flank and left buttock, 2) abrasions present over left thigh, 3) multiple abrasions present dorsal aspect of right hand, left elbow with puncture wound present over left elbow, 4)
abrasions present over left leg and 5) displaced fracture with avulsion base of distal phalanx of right hand ring finger.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations,
it can safely be held that, the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA- 05-MY-5409 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 23-07-2021 at about 7:00 Ravindra Alias Ravindra Kumar vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5793441/

No.KA-05-MY-5409.

sentences.text: Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and he has sustained grievous injury in the said accident.

The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained 1) abrasions present over the left flank and left buttock, 2)
abrasions present over left thigh,
3) multiple abrasions present dorsal aspect of right hand, left elbow with puncture wound present over left elbow, 4) abrasions present over left leg and 5) displaced fracture with avulsion base of distal phalanx of right hand ring finger and for the said injuries he has taken conservative treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
But, there is no evidence placed on record by the petitioner for the purpose of assessing the above pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

In such circumstances,
there is no other option before this Court, except to consider global compensation in general.

20. As per Ex.P.7 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained 1) abrasions present over the left flank and left buttock, 2) abrasions present over left thigh, 3) multiple abrasions present dorsal aspect of right hand, left elbow with puncture wound present over left elbow, 4) abrasions present over left leg and 5) displaced fracture with avulsion base of distal phalanx of right hand ring finger.
The above said injuries No.1 to 4 are simple in nature and injury No. 5 is grievous in nature and he has taken conservative treatment in Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, the petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,70,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced inpatient bill, as per Ex.P.12.
The said bill has been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spend total amount of Rs.10,372/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,372/- under the head of medical expenses.
21. Further, the petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, earlier to the accident he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to accidental injuries he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.

Further, he has neither examined any doctor, nor he has produced any document to show that, due to injuries sustained in the said accident he has suffered any permanent physical disability or deformity and thereby he has lost his earning capacity or he is not in a position to perform his day to day activities.
Such being the case, it is difficult to ascertain pain and sufferings, loss of income during the laid off period, loss of amenities etc.
But, due to above injuries definitely the petitioner would have suffered some pain and sufferings and the same would have been nourished with nutritious food and
he might have
Ravindra
Alias Ravindra Kumar vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5793441/
7 attended with the attendants during the treatment period and he might have spent some amount for conveyance.

In such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, the nature of injuries sustained by him, on humanitarian ground, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for some reasonable compensation.

Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, awarding global compensation of Rs.75,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, to the petitioner, would be just, fair and reasonable compensation and it would meet the ends of justice.
22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.

As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy, the policy bearing No.991491823740007118 issued by the respondent No.3 in respect offending Toyota Innova Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409 was valid from 15-10- 2018 to 14-10-2021.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident.
Further as per Ex.R.1, the respondent No.1, who was the driver of the offending vehicle, was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1/driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/-
from the respondent No.3, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees seventy five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
Entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner, through e- payment on proper identification and verification.

6 p.m., on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, in front of Chambenahalli Gate, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations,
it can safely be held that, the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA- 05-MY-5409 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
But, there is no evidence placed on record by the petitioner for the purpose of assessing the above pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
In such circumstances,
there is no other option before this Court, except to consider global compensation in general.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
Such being the case, it is difficult to ascertain pain and sufferings, loss of income during the laid off period, loss of amenities etc.
Alias Ravindra Kumar vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5793441/
In such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, the nature of injuries sustained by him, on humanitarian ground, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for some reasonable compensation.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, awarding global compensation of Rs.75,000/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization, to the petitioner, would be just, fair and reasonable compensation and it would meet the ends of justice.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1/driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.75,000/-
from the respondent No.3, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees seventy five thousand only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.
Entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner, through e- payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
